sanskrit: kṣatriyasya pramattasya doṣaḥ saṃjāyate mahān adharmāḥ saṃpravartante prajāsaṃkarakārakāḥ
english: When a kṣatriya grows heedless, a great fault is born of it: lawless deeds break loose that throw the people into confusion and ruin.

sanskrit: aśīte vidyate śītaṃ śīte śītaṃ na vidyate avṛṣṭir ativṛṣṭiś ca vyādhiś cāviśati prajāḥ
english: Cold sets in when it should be warm, and in the cold season the cold fails; drought comes, then flood, and sickness invades the people.

sanskrit: nakṣatrāṇy upatiṣṭhanti grahā ghorās tathāpare utpātāś cātra dṛśyante bahavo rājanāśanāḥ
english: The lunar mansions turn baleful, and dread planets likewise rise against him; and many portents are seen abroad that spell a king's undoing.

sanskrit: arakṣitātmā yo rājā prajāś cāpi na rakṣati prajāś ca tasya kṣīyante tāś ca so 'nu vinaśyati
english: The king who does not guard himself, and does not guard his people either—his subjects waste away, and he in turn perishes after them.

sanskrit: dvāv ādadāte hy ekasya dvayoś ca bahavo 'pare kumāryaḥ saṃpralupyante tadāhur nṛpadūṣaṇam
english: Two men seize what belongs to one, and many others seize from those two; maidens are carried off by force—this, they say, is the defilement of a king.

sanskrit: mamaitad iti naikasya manuṣyeṣv avatiṣṭhate tyaktvā dharmaṃ yadā rājā pramādam anutiṣṭhati
english: 'This is mine'—such a claim holds firm for no single man, when the king forsakes dharma and follows the path of heedlessness.

sanskrit: utathya uvāca kālavarṣī ca parjanyo dharmacārī ca pārthivaḥ saṃpad yadaiṣā bhavati sā bibharti sukhaṃ prajāḥ
english: Utathya said: When the rain-cloud pours in its season and the king walks in dharma—when this fortune comes to pass, it sustains the people in happiness.

sanskrit: yo na jānāti nirhantuṃ vastrāṇāṃ rajako malam raktāni vā śodhayituṃ yathā nāsti tathaiva saḥ
english: A washerman who does not know how to strip the soil from garments, nor how to cleanse the dyed cloth, is as good as no washerman at all.

sanskrit: evam eva dvijendrāṇāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ viśām api śūdrāś caturṇāṃ varṇānāṃ nānākarmasv avasthitāḥ
english: Just so the foremost brāhmaṇas, the kṣatriyas, the vaiśyas, and the śūdras—the four varṇas—are each set to their several appointed tasks.

sanskrit: karma śūdre kṛṣir vaiśye daṇḍanītiś ca rājani brahmacaryaṃ tapo mantrāḥ satyaṃ cāpi dvijātiṣu
english: Service belongs to the śūdra, husbandry to the vaiśya, and the rule of the rod to the king; chastity, austerity, the sacred verses, and truth belong to the twice-born.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ yaḥ kṣatriyo veda vastrāṇām iva śodhanam śīladoṣān vinirhantuṃ sa pitā sa prajāpatiḥ
english: That kṣatriya among them who knows how to scour away faults of conduct, as one scours soiled garments clean, is a father to his people—he is their Prajāpati.

sanskrit: kṛtaṃ tretā dvāparaś ca kaliś ca bharatarṣabha rājavṛttāni sarvāṇi rājaiva yugam ucyate
english: Kṛta, Tretā, Dvāpara, and Kali, O bull of the Bhāratas, are all the workings of the king; the king himself is called the very age.

sanskrit: cāturvarṇyaṃ tathā vedāś cāturāśramyam eva ca sarvaṃ pramuhyate hy etad yadā rājā pramādyati
english: The fourfold order of varṇas, the Vedas, and the four stages of life—all this falls into confusion when the king grows heedless.

sanskrit: rājaiva kartā bhūtānāṃ rājaiva ca vināśakaḥ dharmātmā yaḥ sa kartā syād adharmātmā vināśakaḥ
english: The king alone is the maker of all creatures, and the king alone their destroyer; he whose soul is set on dharma is their maker, and he whose soul is lawless, their destroyer.

sanskrit: rājño bhāryāś ca putrāś ca bāndhavāḥ suhṛdas tathā sametya sarve śocanti yadā rājā pramādyati
english: The king's wives and sons, his kinsmen and his friends, all gather together and grieve when the king grows heedless.

sanskrit: hastino 'śvāś ca gāvaś cāpy uṣṭrāśvataragardabhāḥ adharmavṛtte nṛpatau sarve sīdanti pārthiva
english: Elephants and horses and cattle, camels, mules, and donkeys—all sink into ruin, O prince, when the king's conduct is lawless.

sanskrit: durbalārthaṃ balaṃ sṛṣṭaṃ dhātrā māndhātar ucyate abalaṃ tan mahad bhūtaṃ yasmin sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam
english: For the sake of the weak, O Māndhātṛ, the ordaining Creator brought strength into being—so it is said; for the weak are that great power on which all else rests.

sanskrit: yac ca bhūtaṃ sa bhajate bhūtā ye ca tadanvayāḥ adharmasthe hi nṛpatau sarve sīdanti pārthiva
english: Whatever creature he cherishes, and the creatures that follow in its train—all of them sink into ruin, O prince, when the king stands on the side of unrighteousness.

sanskrit: durbalasya hi yac cakṣur muner āśīviṣasya ca aviṣahyatamaṃ manye mā sma durbalam āsadaḥ
english: The eye of the weak man, like the eye of a sage or of a venomous serpent, I hold to be the hardest of all to withstand: never give offense to the weak.

sanskrit: durbalāṃs tāta budhyethā nityam evāvimānitān mā tvāṃ durbalacakṣūṃṣi pradaheyuḥ sabāndhavam
english: Take heed of the weak, my son, and let them never be despised, lest the eyes of the weak burn you to ashes together with your kinsmen.

sanskrit: na hi durbaladagdhasya kule kiṃ cit prarohati āmūlaṃ nirdahaty eva mā sma durbalam āsadaḥ
english: In the house of one burned by the weak nothing ever springs up again; the fire consumes it down to the very root—so never give offense to the weak.

sanskrit: abalaṃ vai balāc chreyo yac cātibalavad balam balasyābaladagdhasya na kiṃ cid avaśiṣyate
english: The weak is mightier than the strong, even than strength that is overwhelming in its might; for of strength once burned by the weak, nothing whatever remains.

sanskrit: vimānito hatotkruṣṭas trātāraṃ cen na vindati amānuṣakṛtas tatra daṇḍo hanti narādhipam
english: If one who is scorned, struck down, and crying out finds no protector, then a chastisement not wrought by human hand falls there and destroys the king of men.

sanskrit: mā sma tāta bale stheyā bādhiṣṭhā māpi durbalam mā tvā durbalacakṣūṃṣi dhakṣyanty agnir ivāśrayam
english: Do not, my son, take your stand upon mere force, nor oppress the weak, lest the eyes of the weak consume you as fire consumes the dwelling that gives it shelter.

sanskrit: yāni mithyābhiśastānāṃ patanty aśrūṇi rodatām tāni putrān paśūn ghnanti teṣāṃ mithyābhiśāsatām
english: The tears that fall from those falsely accused as they weep—those tears slay the sons and the cattle of the men who lay false charges upon them.

sanskrit: yadi nātmani putreṣu na cet pautreṣu naptṛṣu na hi pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ karma sadyaḥ phalati gaur iva
english: If not upon a man himself, then upon his sons, and if not upon his sons, then upon his grandsons and their offspring; for a sinful deed once done does not ripen at once, like a cow whose calf takes time to grow.

sanskrit: yatrābalo vadhyamānas trātāraṃ nādhigacchati mahān daivakṛtas tatra daṇḍaḥ patati dāruṇaḥ
english: Where a weak man, set upon and slain, finds no protector, there a great and terrible chastisement, wrought by fate, comes down.

sanskrit: yuktā yadā jānapadā bhikṣante brāhmaṇā iva abhīkṣṇaṃ bhikṣudoṣeṇa rājānaṃ ghnanti tādṛśāḥ
english: When the country folk, hard-pressed, take to begging like brāhmaṇas, then again and again, by the taint of their beggary, such men bring destruction on the king.

sanskrit: rājño yadā janapade bahavo rājapūruṣāḥ anayenopavartante tad rājñaḥ kilbiṣaṃ mahat
english: When in a king's domain many of the king's officers conduct themselves by misrule, that is a great sin laid upon the king.

sanskrit: yadā yuktā nayanty arthān kāmād arthavaśena vā kṛpaṇaṃ yācamānānāṃ tad rājño vaiśasaṃ mahat
english: When the appointed officers carry off the goods of those who beg piteously, whether out of lust or in greed for gain, that is a great slaughter charged against the king.

sanskrit: mahāvṛkṣo jāyate vardhate ca; taṃ caiva bhūtāni samāśrayanti yadā vṛkṣaś chidyate dahyate vā; tadāśrayā aniketā bhavanti
english: A great tree springs up and grows, and creatures take their shelter beneath it; but when the tree is cut down or burned, those that sheltered there are left without a home.

sanskrit: yadā rāṣṭre dharmam agryaṃ caranti; saṃskāraṃ vā rājaguṇaṃ bruvāṇāḥ tair evādharmaś carito dharmamohāt; tūrṇaṃ jahyāt sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ ca
english: When men in the realm practice what they proclaim to be the highest dharma, or the rite, or the royal virtue, and yet through delusion as to dharma practice unrighteousness in its very name, one should swiftly abandon such deeds, both well done and ill.

sanskrit: yatra pāpā jñāyamānāś caranti; satāṃ kalir vindati tatra rājñaḥ yadā rājā śāsti narān naśiṣyān; na tad rājyaṃ vardhate bhūmipāla
english: Where the wicked, known for what they are, go about freely, there strife befalls the king's good men; when a king chastises men who are not deserving of it, that kingdom does not prosper, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: yaś cāmātyaṃ mānayitvā yathārhaṃ; mantre ca yuddhe ca nṛpo niyuñjyāt pravardhate tasya rāṣṭraṃ nṛpasya; bhuṅkte mahīṃ cāpy akhilāṃ cirāya
english: But the king who honors his minister as he deserves and sets him to his task in counsel and in war—that king's realm grows great, and he enjoys the whole earth for a long age.

sanskrit: atrāpi sukṛtaṃ karma vācaṃ caiva subhāṣitām samīkṣya pūjayan rājā dharmaṃ prāpnoty anuttamam
english: Here too the king who discerns a deed well done and a word well spoken, and honors them, attains the highest dharma.

sanskrit: saṃvibhajya yadā bhuṅkte na cānyān avamanyate nihanti balinaṃ dṛptaṃ sa rājño dharma ucyate
english: When he shares before he himself enjoys, and despises no man, and strikes down the strong man grown insolent—that is called the dharma of a king.

sanskrit: trāyate hi yadā sarvaṃ vācā kāyena karmaṇā putrasyāpi na mṛṣyec ca sa rājño dharma ucyate
english: When he protects all by word, by body, and by deed, and will not condone a wrong even in his own son—that is called the dharma of a king.

sanskrit: yadā śāraṇikān rājā putravat parirakṣati bhinatti na ca maryādāṃ sa rājño dharma ucyate
english: When the king guards those who have sought his refuge as though they were his sons, and never breaks the bounds of right—that is called the dharma of a king.

sanskrit: yadāptadakṣiṇair yajñair yajate śraddhayānvitaḥ kāmadveṣāv anādṛtya sa rājño dharma ucyate
english: When, filled with faith, he sacrifices with rites whose priestly fees are duly paid, heedless of desire and hatred—that is called the dharma of a king.

sanskrit: kṛpaṇānāthavṛddhānāṃ yadāśru vyapamārṣṭi vai harṣaṃ saṃjanayan nṝṇāṃ sa rājño dharma ucyate
english: When he wipes away the tears of the wretched, the helpless, and the aged, and kindles gladness in his people—that is called the dharma of a king.

sanskrit: vivardhayati mitrāṇi tathārīṃś cāpakarṣati saṃpūjayati sādhūṃś ca sa rājño dharma ucyate
english: When he increases his friends and draws down his foes, and pays honor to the good—that is called the dharma of a king.

sanskrit: satyaṃ pālayati prāptyā nityaṃ bhūmiṃ prayacchati pūjayaty atithīn bhṛtyān sa rājño dharma ucyate
english: When he keeps his word faithfully, ever bestows land in due measure, and honors guests and dependents—that is called the dharma of a king.

sanskrit: nigrahānugrahau cobhau yatra syātāṃ pratiṣṭhitau asmiṃl loke pare caiva rājā tat prāpnute phalam
english: Where both restraint and favor are firmly established, the king gains the fruit thereof in this world and in the next.

sanskrit: yamo rājā dhārmikāṇāṃ māndhātaḥ parameśvaraḥ saṃyacchan bhavati prāṇān nasaṃyacchaṃs tu pāpakaḥ
english: Yama, the supreme lord, O Māndhātṛ, is the king of the righteous when he holds living beings in due restraint; but when he restrains them not, he turns to evil.

sanskrit: ṛtvikpurohitācāryān satkṛtyānavamanya ca yadā samyak pragṛhṇāti sa rājño dharma ucyate
english: When he honors the officiating priests, the family chaplain, and the teachers, and never slights them but rightly upholds them—that is called the dharma of a king.

sanskrit: yamo yacchati bhūtāni sarvāṇy evāviśeṣataḥ tasya rājñānukartavyaṃ yantavyā vidhivat prajāḥ
english: Yama holds all beings in check without distinction; the king should do as he does, and govern his people according to the ordinance.

sanskrit: sahasrākṣeṇa rājā hi sarva evopamīyate sa paśyati hi yaṃ dharmaṃ sa dharmaḥ puruṣarṣabha
english: Every king is likened to the thousand-eyed Indra; for whatever dharma he beholds, that, O bull among men, is dharma.

sanskrit: apramādena śikṣethāḥ kṣamāṃ buddhiṃ dhṛtiṃ matim bhūtānāṃ sattvajijñāsāṃ sādhv asādhu ca sarvadā
english: With unwavering care learn forbearance, understanding, steadfastness, and judgment, and the discernment of the true nature of creatures, of good and evil, always.

sanskrit: saṃgrahaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ dānaṃ ca madhurā ca vāk paurajānapadāś caiva goptavyāḥ svā yathā prajāḥ
english: The winning of all creatures, generosity, and gentle speech—and the townsfolk and the country folk are to be protected as one's own people.

sanskrit: na jātv adakṣo nṛpatiḥ prajāḥ śaknoti rakṣitum bhāro hi sumahāṃs tāta rājyaṃ nāma suduṣkaram
english: Never can an unskilled king protect his subjects; for it is a very great burden, my son—kingship, so they call it, is exceedingly hard to bear.

sanskrit: tad daṇḍavin nṛpaḥ prājñaḥ śūraḥ śaknoti rakṣitum na hi śakyam adaṇḍena klībenābuddhināpi vā
english: A king who is wise, valiant, and versed in the rod can protect them; it cannot be done by one who lacks the rod, who is unmanly, or who is without understanding.

sanskrit: abhirūpaiḥ kule jātair dakṣair bhaktair bahuśrutaiḥ sarvā buddhīḥ parīkṣethās tāpasāśramiṇām api
english: With men of fitting bearing, well born, skilled, devoted, and deeply learned, you should test out all counsels—even those of the ascetics in their hermitages.

sanskrit: tatas tvaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ dharmaṃ vetsyasi vai param svadeśe paradeśe vā na te dharmo vinaśyati
english: Then you will come to know the highest dharma of all beings; and whether in your own land or another's, your dharma will not be lost.

sanskrit: dharmaś cārthaś ca kāmaś ca dharma evottaro bhavet asmiṃl loke pare caiva dharmavit sukham edhate
english: Of dharma, artha, and kāma, let dharma ever be the highest; for in this world and the next, the one who knows dharma flourishes in happiness.

sanskrit: tyajanti dārān prāṇāṃś ca manuṣyāḥ pratipūjitāḥ saṃgrahaś caiva bhūtānāṃ dānaṃ ca madhurā ca vāk
english: Men, when they are duly honored, will give up wife and life itself; the winning of creatures lies in generosity and in gentle speech.

sanskrit: apramādaś ca śaucaṃ ca tāta bhūtikaraṃ mahat etebhyaś caiva māndhātaḥ satataṃ mā pramādithāḥ
english: Vigilance and purity, my son, work great prosperity; and from these, O Māndhātṛ, never at any time fall away into heedlessness.

sanskrit: apramatto bhaved rājā chidradarśī parātmanoḥ nāsya chidraṃ paraḥ paśyec chidreṣu param anviyāt
english: Let the king be ever watchful, marking the weak points of his foe and of himself; let no enemy spy out a weak point in him, while he himself seeks out his enemy's weak points.

sanskrit: etad vṛttaṃ vāsavasya yamasya varuṇasya ca rājarṣīṇāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ tat tvam apy anupālaya
english: Such was the conduct of Vāsava, of Yama, and of Varuṇa, and of all the royal sages: do you too uphold it.

sanskrit: tat kuruṣva mahārāja vṛttaṃ rājarṣisevitam ātiṣṭha divyaṃ panthānam ahnāya bharatarṣabha
english: Do that, O great king—that course which the royal sages have followed; set your feet without delay upon the heavenly path, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: dharmavṛttaṃ hi rājānaṃ pretya ceha ca bhārata devarṣipitṛgandharvāḥ kīrtayanty amitaujasaḥ
english: For a king of righteous conduct, O Bhārata, in the world hereafter and in this one, the gods, the sages, the fathers, and the gandharvas, boundless in might, sing his praise.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sa evam ukto māndhātā tenotathyena bhārata kṛtavān aviśaṅkas tad ekaḥ prāpa ca medinīm
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed by Utathya, O Bhārata, Māndhātṛ acted on it without a doubt, and he alone won the whole earth.

sanskrit: bhavān api tathā samyaṅ māndhāteva mahīpatiḥ dharmaṃ kṛtvā mahīṃ rakṣan svarge sthānam avāpsyasi
english: You too, like Māndhātṛ the lord of the earth, by rightly practicing dharma and guarding the earth, will gain a place in heaven.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃ dharme sthātum icchan rājā varteta dhārmikaḥ pṛcchāmi tvā kuruśreṣṭha tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How should a righteous king, wishing to stand firm in dharma, conduct himself? This I ask you, O best of the Kurus; tell it to me, grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam gītaṃ dṛṣṭārthatattvena vāmadevena dhīmatā
english: Bhīṣma said: On this they tell an ancient tale, sung by the wise Vāmadeva, who had perceived the very truth of things.

sanskrit: rājā vasumanā nāma kausalyo balavāñ śuciḥ maharṣiṃ paripapraccha vāmadevaṃ yaśasvinam
english: A king named Vasumanas, ruler of the Kosalas, mighty and pure, questioned the great sage, the renowned Vāmadeva.

sanskrit: dharmārthasahitaṃ vākyaṃ bhagavann anuśādhi mām yena vṛttena vai tiṣṭhan na cyaveyaṃ svadharmataḥ
english: 'Instruct me, blessed one, with words that hold both dharma and artha—by what conduct, standing firm, I may not fall away from my own dharma.'

sanskrit: tam abravīd vāmadevas tapasvī japatāṃ varaḥ hemavarṇam upāsīnaṃ yayātim iva nāhuṣam
english: To him spoke Vāmadeva, that ascetic, foremost of those who murmur the sacred prayers, as the king sat attending upon him, golden-hued, like Yayāti the son of Nahuṣa.

sanskrit: dharmam evānuvartasva na dharmād vidyate param dharme sthitā hi rājāno jayanti pṛthivīm imām
english: Follow dharma alone, for nothing higher than dharma is known; for it is kings established in dharma who conquer this earth.

sanskrit: arthasiddheḥ paraṃ dharmaṃ manyate yo mahīpatiḥ ṛtāṃ ca kurute buddhiṃ sa dharmeṇa virocate
english: The king who holds dharma higher than the winning of wealth, and makes his understanding true, shines forth by his dharma.

sanskrit: adharmadarśī yo rājā balād eva pravartate kṣipram evāpayāto 'smād ubhau prathamamadhyamau
english: The king whose vision is set on unrighteousness, who acts by sheer force, swiftly falls away from this world, losing both the first end and the middle.

sanskrit: asatpāpiṣṭhasacivo vadhyo lokasya dharmahā sahaiva parivāreṇa kṣipram evāvasīdati
english: The slayer of dharma, with wicked and basest counselors, fit for the world to put to death, swiftly sinks to ruin together with his whole retinue.

sanskrit: arthānām ananuṣṭhātā kāmacārī vikatthanaḥ api sarvāṃ mahīṃ labdhvā kṣipram eva vinaśyati
english: He who attends not to his proper aims, who follows his own whim and boasts loudly, though he win the whole earth, swiftly comes to destruction.

sanskrit: athādadānaḥ kalyāṇam anasūyur jitendriyaḥ vardhate matimān rājā srotobhir iva sāgaraḥ
english: But the wise king who takes hold of what is good, free of malice and master of his senses, grows great, as the ocean grows by its inflowing streams.

sanskrit: na pūrṇo 'smīti manyeta dharmataḥ kāmato 'rthataḥ buddhito mitrataś cāpi satataṃ vasudhādhipaḥ
english: Let the lord of the earth never think, 'I am full'—neither in dharma, nor in desire, nor in wealth, nor in understanding, nor in friends—at any time.

sanskrit: eteṣv eva hi sarveṣu lokayātrā pratiṣṭhitā etāni śṛṇvaṃl labhate yaśaḥ kīrtiṃ śriyaḥ prajāḥ
english: For upon all these the course of the world is founded; and one who gives ear to these gains glory, renown, fortunes, and subjects.

sanskrit: evaṃ yo dharmasaṃrambhī dharmārthaparicintakaḥ arthān samīkṣyārabhate sa dhruvaṃ mahad aśnute
english: Thus the king who is zealous for dharma, who ponders well both dharma and artha, and who undertakes his ventures after due reflection, surely attains greatness.

sanskrit: adātā hy anatisneho daṇḍenāvartayan prajāḥ sāhasaprakṛtī rājā kṣipram eva vinaśyati
english: The king who gives nothing, who shows no warmth, who drives his people on with the rod and is rash by nature, swiftly comes to destruction.

sanskrit: atha pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ buddhyā na ca paśyaty abuddhimān akīrtyāpi samāyukto mṛto narakam aśnute
english: And the fool who does evil knowingly yet does not see it, burdened with infamy besides, when dead attains to hell.

sanskrit: atha mānayitur dātuḥ śuklasya rasavedinaḥ vyasanaṃ svam ivotpannaṃ vijighāṃsanti mānavāḥ
english: But of the king who honors others, who gives, who is upright and knows the savor of things, when calamity befalls him men long to ward it off as though it were their own.

sanskrit: yasya nāsti gurur dharme na cānyān anupṛcchati sukhatantro 'rthalābheṣu na ciraṃ mahad aśnute
english: He who has no teacher in dharma and asks no counsel of others, who is given over to ease in his pursuit of gain, does not long enjoy greatness.
